params.title: Getting around
params.subtitle: The workspace, editing, dictation and the agent

runs.t: Under the slide: the thumbnails, in a strip a toolbar button hides or shows. Click one to show it, drag it to move it, + adds one from a layout.
In the middle: the slide, exactly as it prints. Select, move and edit elements right on it.
On the right: the conversation with the agent and the dictation draft. Top right, the menu: present, open, help. Everything else, app settings included, you ask the agent.
: selects an element, or a field (title, kicker…).
: edits the text. One line per paragraph; a leading “- ” makes a bullet.
: move or resize a free element, cell by cell on the grid.

: one button opens the add grid, with one section per pack of the deck (text, card, shape, chart and table from the base pack, then each widget pack), filtered by name, label or description; undo, redo.

: a data table edited, like a chart, in the agent's dock while it is selected, with the same grid. Toggle the header row, the first column as header and striped rows; align each column (automatic puts numbers at the end). A table larger than its box shrinks to fit. “Show as a chart” and “Show as a table” switch between the two, keeping the data, in one undo step.
: an element, or text from elsewhere, which becomes a text element.
: ⌘Z reverts the whole last gesture, whatever it was.
: 12 × 6 cells by default, set in the layout. Snapping is always on; ⌘' shows the nodes.
: “New slide” offers the layouts of the deck's layout packs (Essentiel, or your own).

: ask the agent for the workshop. The pack opens as a deck with one slide per layout. A library pack opens in its own tab; closing it (“Done” or the tab’s ×) offers to update the deck if the pack changed, otherwise the update waits in “Deck packs”. While that tab is open, no other tab changes the pack. An imported deck’s own pack opens in the deck’s tab, and “Done” brings the deck back.
: in pack mode, the Widgets section of the pile opens their Typst code, with a live preview.

: Papier, Pro, Neutre or your own. Say or type “theme” alone: each theme shows on your slide, without waiting for the agent; hover to preview, click to apply. Ask the agent to suggest a theme: it opens the same picker. It is independent of the layout packs. “Open”, on the theme’s row in “Deck packs”, opens it in its own tab: sample slides, one per Essentiel layout, show the draft, and the panel sets its tokens one by one and shows what it extends. The tab saves on its own; “Done” closes it. Editing Papier, Pro or Neutre creates a variant that extends it, to pick next in the theme picker; your own theme gets a new version, which each deck takes from “Deck packs”. While that tab is open, no other tab changes the theme. The extends list can be reordered, and parents can be added or removed there.
: the toolbar button opens the deck’s packs, listed by kind (layouts, widgets, theme). It shows a mark when one of your versions differs from the deck’s.
: if the deck uses an older, newer or parallel version of a pack, “Use my version” switches the deck to yours and “Make theirs my version” keeps the deck’s as yours. Both can be undone.
: “Add from the library” pins a pack in the deck; “Remove” unpins it, unless a slide or another pack still needs it. The base pack always stays.
: it starts from the widgets of each pack, with their starting content. A layout with free slots accepts only the kinds it allows.
: the deck’s theme is picked here too, with its extends list: parents apply first, later ones win, and you can add, remove or reorder them. “Open” opens it in its own tab to edit it.
: Whisper runs locally; the model downloads once, the first time you press the mic.

: pick API in the dictation settings; each sentence goes to an OpenAI-compatible service, with the key read from an environment variable. Only you set the API address (https, or http for this computer) and the key variable (a name like OPENAI_API_KEY), in the settings box. An app opened from the Finder does not see shell variables: set the key with `launchctl setenv OPENAI_API_KEY …` or start the app from a terminal. For Azure OpenAI or a gateway, add query parameters (`api-version=…`) and headers (`api-key: $AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`; `$NAME` reads a variable), and leave the key variable empty to send no Bearer.

: the ⚙ of the dictation bar opens the dictation and agent settings in the agent area. They stay open until you close them and follow every change. The agent can open and change them when you ask; switching to the API, a download and an agent switch ask you first, and an agent switch waits until no reply runs.
: each pause ends a sentence, transcribed with the deck's vocabulary as context.
At the cursor or in the draft
: while editing a text, ⌘D writes at the cursor; otherwise it goes to the draft.
: review, fix, then Send to the agent (⌘↩). A pause never decides for you.
One agent turn is a single ⌘Z entry. It has no files and no terminal: only Oku Slides' tools.
Saving, opening, deleting a set, changing a setting: it asks, and you must click, never Enter.
Questions in a card under the element (1–4, Enter, E, Esc), variants in a drawer, live settings in a sticky note.

⧉ at the top of the thread (or Window › Agent in a separate window, on macOS) opens the agent in its own window, to place on a second screen. It follows the active tab of the window in front. Attach, or closing the window, brings it back to the right column, any typing in progress kept in the draft.
: every change goes to the file; a new deck goes to Documents/Oku Slides.
: one deck per tab, several windows; everything comes back at next launch.
: ask the agent for the history. A slider walks every version in the file; Restore makes one current again.
: two copies of the same deck, edited separately, merge without conflicts (ask the agent to merge the other PDF).
: ⌘? opens this deck, read-only, in the interface language.
: ⌘O on a .pptx, or opening it from the Finder, shows “Import a PowerPoint presentation”. The resulting deck comes up in a new tab.
: keeps the original look: the deck pins the Neutre theme and carries its own tokens, with layouts made for this presentation.
: rebuilds the slides with layout packs and a theme from the library.
: the agent compares each slide with a render of the original and corrects the gaps. Greyed out, with the reason, when no agent is usable.
: frozen as an image and listed in the import report, which the agent reads.
: the workshop, asked of the agent, edits its layouts, saved in this presentation only; its look stays in the deck’s own tokens, over the Neutre theme.
: [import] in config.toml, max_input_mib (largest file) and witness (office2pdf or soffice, the reference render).
Go to tab n (9: the last)
Move by one cell, or by 1 pt
Move the item along the list axis
: overrides any key of config.toml; a double underscore goes down one level, so OKU_SLIDES_STT__VAD__PAUSE=1.0 sets pause in [stt.vad].
: the built-in defaults, then config.toml in the app data folder, then the variables; the last one wins.
: settings are read once; restart the app after changing a variable.
, such as [import] soffice, can only be set in config.toml: as a variable, the settings are invalid and the app does not start.
: opened from the Dock, the Finder or a desktop menu, the app does not see your shell's variables. Start it from a terminal, or on macOS run launchctl setenv NAME value before opening it.
: the app data folder, config.toml included (macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/me.dartiguenave.oku-slides; Linux: ~/.local/share/…; Windows: %APPDATA%\…).
: where new decks save themselves (default Documents/Oku Slides).
: dictation and local agent models, and the dictation settings (config.json).
: your widget packs, layout packs and themes.
: the interface language (en, fr, de, ja…); default: the system's.
: light or dark; default: the system's.
: the name written in the history of decks you edit.
: false checks only through Check for Updates…; a development build never checks by itself.
: office2pdf or soffice, the reference rendering of a faithful import.
: address of the oku-slides serve dev server (127.0.0.1:4870).
: the agent, a key of [agent.presets] (claude, codex, gemini, local); the agent choice is then locked. An unknown key stops the launch.
: auto or gguf, the engine of the local agent.
: false keeps Whisper only, without Apple's engine.
: the pause that ends a sentence (s), like every [stt.vad] key.
: a WAV file replayed instead of the microphone.
: the variable named in the dictation settings (OPENAI_API_KEY by default) and each $VARIABLE of its headers, read when dictation starts, never stored.
(its account, its key): the agent inherits the app's environment.
, or USERPROFILE when HOME is not set: the base of the default folders.
on Linux, APPDATA on Windows: the parent of the app data folder.
: your name in the deck history when [author] name is not set.
(Linux): the system language, default of the interface and of dictation.
: finds the agents' programs (npx…) and LibreOffice (soffice).
: the proxy of model downloads and of the dictation API (never for an API on this computer).
(Linux): certificates are the system's; a company proxy's authority must be installed there.
: the log level, in development builds only, such as RUST_LOG=info,ureq=debug for the network; a release logs at info, on the standard error.
(Linux): set by AppImage, the app installs its updates; without it, it only tells you about them.
(Linux): without a session bus, a second launch opens a second app.
: marks the app's own render process; never set it.

params.title: The Typst library
params.subtitle: oku-slides: structured slides, driven by tokens

runs.t: : title, contents, chapters, content slides with header and footer, end.
: element frames are given in points.
: all styling goes through them; a theme is just a set of tokens.
: hand-written Typst, or the app's JSON deck through render-deck.
: the library, its themes (papier, pro) and its examples.
Opens a chapter: feeds contents and header
Content: default, columns, split, center, quote
Free page, with or without header and footer
Card with an accent rule; highlight puts it on dark
title, subtitle, author, date, organization, logo, lang
then #var("client") in content, or {{client}} in titles, parameters and JSON texts.
: default-tokens ← component defaults of each pack (component.<namespace>.*) ← theme chain ← tokens. Objects merge key by key; any other value, a list included, replaces the one below.
: hex or another colour's name; fallback families.
size, space, radius, stroke, weight, leading
: in pt (em for leading), or another token's name.

: owned by packs. card and table under component.base.*; title, title-slide, chapter, toc, end-slide, quote and columns under component.essentiel.*. header, footer, list and kicker are global families, outside component.

: papier (Newsreader, Instrument Sans, sage green), pro (Inter, navy and cyan) and neutre (no tokens of its own, for imported decks). A theme has a namespace and an ordered extends list: parents apply first, later ones win, a list replaces.
: each slide and element of the JSON deck names its widget (kind).

: essentiel/title, essentiel/toc, essentiel/chapter, essentiel/content, essentiel/end, essentiel/blank, from the built-in essentiel pack. The element widgets (base/text, base/card, base/image, base/shape, base/chart, base/table, base/stack) come from the built-in base pack.
: one file per widget, widgets/<name>.typ; shared code goes in widgets/_commun.typ.
: a widget that does not compile is set aside with its diagnostics; the others stay.
: a widget reads its colours and sizes from tokens (color-of, size-of).
#import "/oku-slides/lib.typ": widget, field, fields-stack, params as p, color-of, size-of
render gets (args, ctx); ctx carries id, tokens, vars, style, framed and load (the host's images and charts).
One line; bind ties it to the deck
Tags a parameter's box (<oku-slides-field>): this is what makes a widget's text editable in place. To stack fields, use fields-stack rather than stack.
A deck pins several widget packs, each under its own namespace. A pack widget is named namespace/name and never replaces a base widget.
p.list(item: …, item-label:, min:, max:, default:) declares repeated items with typed columns: plain, rich, number, flag, choice, asset. Render each with list-item, fields with field(c, …).

In the widget editor, a table: add, remove, reorder (⌥↑/↓ on a row), paste TSV. On the slide, an item moves with the keyboard from one of its fields; for the rest, ask the agent, which edits by id with edit_list.

params.title: The .oku-slides.pdf format
params.subtitle: An ordinary PDF that keeps its sources

params.title: A PDF that carries its sources

runs.t: Any PDF reader shows and prints it. The sources do not show up among its attachments.
Oku Slides reads back the deck, its images, fonts and packs, with its whole history.
oku-slides strip removes the sources: what remains is a PDF without history.
The catalog's page-piece dictionary (ISO 32000, § 14.5): a private stream, checked against its SHA-256 digest.
deck.loro                       full snapshot of the deck's Loro replica
widgets/<hex>/widgets/<name>.typ one file per widget, _commun included
layouts/<hex>/layouts/<name>.typ one file per layout, _commun included
themes/<hex>/theme.json         one file per pinned theme version (the theme and its extends closure)
<hex>: SHA-256 of the content. An image is named sha256:<hex> in the deck.

params.title: The deck is a Loro CRDT

runs.t: : every past version can be viewed and restored from the PDF alone.
: two copies edited apart recombine; a PDF changed on disk is merged on save.
: the v9 JSON deck is the canonical read-back of the replica.

: ordered lists with ids (items, data), prose, rich prose with marks, and the rest last-writer-wins. Slides and their elements form a single tree: moving an element between slots or slides keeps concurrent edits, and undoing a removal brings back the same element.
A free element has a frame { x, y, w, h } in pt, or a grid cell. The operations schema: oku-slides schema.
Envelope /Version 2, zip version 12. Older: ignored, the PDF opens like any other PDF. Newer: refused.
History: 32 MiB; decompressed sources: 256 MiB. Adjustable under [sources] in config.toml. A deleted element is erased for good after 30 days of activity on the deck (compact_after_days).
